topic: How a drilled water well works, built one part at a time from a drill and a patch of dirt

hook.say: You're building the hole 43 million Americans drink from. Before dinner, it fails 5 ways. How do you stop it?

beats.say: Water hides underground in sand and rock layers called aquifers. So you drill down to one. That's the borehole.
beats.label: BOREHOLE

beats.say: But loose ground caves in. So you slide a pipe down the hole. That's the casing.
beats.label: CASING
beats.creates: rain seeps down the outside of the pipe

beats.say: Now rain seeps down the outside of the pipe. So you fill the gap with cement or clay. That's the grout seal.
beats.label: GROUT SEAL
beats.creates: sand comes in with the water

beats.say: In sandy ground, water drags sand in. So a slotted pipe holds the sand back, like a strainer. That's the well screen.
beats.label: WELL SCREEN
beats.creates: the water sits too deep to reach
beats.solves: sand comes in with the water

beats.say: Now the water sits far below. A pump built for underwater work pushes it up. That's the submersible pump.
beats.label: SUBMERSIBLE PUMP
beats.creates: the pump starts every time you pour a glass

beats.say: Now the pump starts whenever you pour a glass. So a tank holds pressurized water. That's the pressure tank.
beats.label: PRESSURE TANK
beats.solves: the pump starts every time you pour a glass

payoff.say: You built a water well. The neighbor brings a bucket.
payoff.title: YOU BUILT A WELL.
payoff.subtitle: ONE PROBLEM AT A TIME

ask.say: Save this for when someone asks where well water comes from.

original_element: The build itself: a cutaway of a drilled well where every part is added on screen to fix the exact problem the previous part caused.

sources.claim: More than 43 million people in the US (about 15 percent) rely on private wells for drinking water
sources.source: USGS, What's in Your Well Water? (usgs.gov/mission-areas/water-resources/science/domestic-private-supply-wells); USGS Circular 1360 summary (usgs.gov/programs/environmental-health-program/science/groundwater-quality-principal-aquifers-united-states); EPA, About Private Water Wells (about 15 percent of Americans)

sources.claim: 5 = our own count of the problems shown after the water is found: hole caves in, rain seeps down, sand comes in, water too deep, pump keeps starting. 6 = our own count of the parts built.
Aquifers are water-bearing rock or sediment that yields water to wells
sources.source: USGS Water Science School, Aquifers and Groundwater, usgs.gov/water-science-school/science/aquifers-and-groundwater; Maine Geological Survey, Sand and Gravel Aquifers

sources.claim: Casing is a steel or plastic pipe that keeps the borehole from caving in
sources.source: University of Arizona Cooperative Extension, Private Water Well Components (az1486b); US EPA Private Well module (PRIV_WELL_Module_508)

sources.claim: Grout (cement or clay) fills the gap between casing and hole to stop surface water running down the outside
sources.source: Washington State WAC 173-160-231 (surface seals); University of Arizona Cooperative Extension az1504; Mississippi State Extension P1815 Wellhead Protection

sources.claim: A well screen lets water in and keeps sand out; used in sand and gravel aquifers, bedrock wells are often open holes
sources.source: University of Arizona Cooperative Extension az1504; Warren County (Ohio) well screens BMP; US EPA Private Well module

sources.claim: A submersible pump sits in the well below the water level and pushes water up
sources.source: University of Nebraska-Lincoln Extension G2152 (2012); University of Arizona Cooperative Extension az1504

sources.claim: A pressure tank stores water under pressure so the pump starts and stops less often
sources.source: University of Nebraska-Lincoln Extension G2152 (2012); University of Arizona Cooperative Extension az1504
